title: Introduce checkpoint manifest & tokenizer splitpoints to simplify loader logic
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The current model loader contains a tangled set of heuristics to support a wide variety of checkpoint formats and shard layouts. Tokenizer boundaries (where encoded token sequences align with weight shard KV ranges and cached prefixes) are inferred at runtime in multiple places, which complicates caching, increases startup latency, and is a common source of subtle bugs during quantized or heterogeneous-shard loads.

Proposed change: Introduce an explicit, versioned checkpoint manifest (checkpoint.manifest.json) that is generated by ingest tooling and bundled with each checkpoint. The manifest will canonicalize: format version, list of shard files with byte/parameter ranges, model graph fingerprint, tokenizer splitpoints (explicit token index boundaries aligned with shard offsets), and compatible runtime hints (preferred kernels, quantization profile id). The loader will first validate and consume the manifest and then perform a deterministic shard-to-offset mapping and tokenizer reconciliation step. This removes duplicated boundary logic from the runtime and gives a single source-of-truth for tooling and migration scripts.

Goals: reduce loader codepaths, lower cold-start latency for large multi-shard checkpoints, remove race conditions in KV cache init, and provide a clear upgrade path for older checkpoints with a migration tool that emits a manifest.

Scope: loader validation + parser changes, manifest schema & generator, migration CLI (checkpoint-migrate --emit-manifest), unit + integration tests, a small UX change in the console to surface manifest warnings. Backwards compatibility: runtime accepts checkpoints with and without manifest for two releases; for older checkpoints the migration tool will be recommended and a best-effort fallback logic retained behind a feature flag.
updates: 2026-03-01 - Spike: implemented a sketch of manifest schema and validated against three internal checkpoints (gpt-small-1, opt-1.3b sharded, and a mixed-quantized 4-shard model). Verified that explicit splitpoints remove the need for runtime token boundary heuristics in the loader. — Mateo

2026-03-03 - Design review: agreed on manifest fields and versioning strategy. Added model_graph_fingerprint and compatible_runtime_hints to support future rollout decisions. Action: Aisha to write spec doc. — PM (Aisha)

2026-03-05 - Perf benchmark: cold-start end-to-end model load time reduced by 18% for a 12-shard checkpoint when manifest is present (benchmark run on p3-equivalent); memory overhead for manifest ~150KB. Recorded in internal dashboard: /dashboards/model-load/eng-20645. — Eng Infra
2026-03-07 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2789 implements manifest parsing, manifest-backed shard map, and migration CLI skeleton. Needs tests for fallback path. — Mateo
2026-03-09 - Security note: manifest contains only metadata and no secrets; discussed with Security and KMS integration unaffected. Marking security_review_required=false. — Security (Lina)
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts checkpoints with manifest and uses manifest-provided shard map for loading
Migration CLI can emit a valid manifest for older checkpoints and validates checksums of produced shard mapping
Unit tests cover tokenizer splitpoint reconciliation logic and KV cache init with manifest vs fallback
Integration test shows <= 5% variance in throughput after change and demonstrates >=10% cold-start latency improvement on multi-shard artifacts
Console surfaces a non-blocking warning for checkpoints without manifest and links to migration docs
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (flagged rollout, runtime-2.3-alpha): Add manifest parsing, keep fallback heuristics behind FEATURE_MANIFEST_FALLBACK flag; run internal canary in staging for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (migration tooling, docs): Ship checkpoint-migrate CLI and Confluence guide; run migration on a subset of internal checkpoints and create manifests
Phase 3 (opt-in for hosted): Expose manifest-warning in Console and offer automated migration for small checkpoints during upload
Phase 4 (remove fallback): After 2 releases of backwards compatibility and customer migration window, remove fallback heuristics and make manifest required
